Theme

Latin word

cōnstāns

cōnstāns, cōnstantis

adjective, third declension

steady, consistent, unchanging; steady, unchanging; steadfast

In this lexicon

  • consistent

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 3.35: rēcta et convenientia et cōnstantia nātūra dēsīderat (Lewis & Short, s.v. conveniō)

  • constant

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. N.D. 3.24: cursūs certī et cōnstantēs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Lael. 62; Traupman 296: constant, cōnstāns; Traupman 296

Examples

  • omnīnō sī quicquam est decōrum, nihil est profectō magis quam aequābilitās ūniversae vītae

    if anything at all is becoming, nothing surely is more so than consistency in the whole of one’s lifeCic. Off. 1.111 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for consistent

  • in Oppiānicō sibi cōnstāre et superiōribus cōnsentīre jūdiciīs dēbuērunt

    in the case of Oppianicus they ought to have been consistent with themselves and agreed with the earlier verdictsCic. Clu. 60 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for consistent

  • sunt igitur firmī et stabilēs et cōnstantēs ēligendī, cujus generis est magna pēnūria

    so we must choose friends who are firm, steady and constant, and of that kind there is a great shortageCic. Lael. 62

    In the entry for constant

  • praeclāraque est aequābilitās in omnī vītā et īdem semper vultus eademque frōns

    and a fine thing is evenness all through life: always the same face, the same browCic. Off. 1.90
